Steering Map

Push one MLP neuron in Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B and watch the whole corpus move. Faint gray is the original map, color is the steered map, and each arrow follows one domain's center. The table gives the real, full-dimensional effect per domain, compared with 30 random neurons from the same layer pushed by the same amount. Style neurons carry toxicity or verse; math neurons were found by gradient × activation on GSM8K word problems.

Both layers are placed with the same saved UMAP model, so position differences come from the push. UMAP snaps new points toward existing neighbourhoods: small moves can look like nothing and large moves get pulled into existing clusters. Read the size of an effect from the table, not from arrow length.

z = distance from the 30 random same-layer neurons at this site and dose, in random-neuron standard deviations. ● = significant after FDR correction across all neurons of the group, doses, sites and domains (q < 0.05).
▲ hit harder / ▼ spared, relative to how hard this push hits the map overall (profile test, q < 0.05).
Toward concept = movement along the neuron's concept direction, in units of the gap between its two sides: toxic − clean or Shakespearean − modern pairs for the style neurons; the math word problem centroid − the centroid of the other domains (arithmetic excluded) for the math neurons.
